lines.flight3d.setting.invert.help: Up on the stick dives, as a pilot's stick does.
lines.flight3d.radio.stay: Stay with me! Their base is past the islands.
lines.flight3d.radio.rings: Rings! Fly through them to mend your shield.
lines.flight3d.radio.tail: I've got one on my tail! Get it off me!
lines.flight3d.radio.behind: More behind us! Hold your fire till they pass.
lines.flight3d.radio.turrets: Turrets on the plateau. Roll to turn their shots aside!
lines.flight3d.radio.flagship: That's their flagship in the bay. Hit the engines first!
lines.flight3d.radio.free: All range mode! Take it down!

notes.flight3d.boot: A step on the loading screen while the game builds the sea, the islands and the enemy's base.
notes.flight3d.setting.invert: A setting in the pause menu: pushing the stick up makes the ship dive, as in a real plane.
notes.flight3d.kestrel: The wingman's call sign (a kestrel is a small falcon), shown as the speaker's name over each radio line.
notes.flight3d.radio.stay: KESTREL, the player's wingman, on the radio: short, urgent calls, like Star Fox 64's. The player flies a fighter toward the enemy's base and its flagship.
notes.flight3d.radio.rings: Silver and gold rings in the sky: flying through one mends the ship's shield.
notes.flight3d.radio.tail: An enemy fighter is chasing KESTREL: the player should shoot it down.
notes.flight3d.radio.behind: Enemy fighters come up from behind and pass the player.
notes.flight3d.radio.turrets: A barrel roll (a spin of the ship) turns enemy shots aside.
notes.flight3d.radio.masts: Tall masts on the base to fly between.
notes.flight3d.radio.flagship: The boss: a big warship in the bay. Its four engines go first, then its core.
notes.flight3d.radio.thanks: The player shot down the fighter chasing KESTREL.
notes.flight3d.radio.core: All four engines are destroyed and the flagship's core is open to fire.
notes.flight3d.radio.free: The rails end: the player now flies freely all round the flagship (Star Fox 64's "all-range mode").
notes.flight3d.radio.hit: The fighter chasing KESTREL was not shot down in time and hit it.
notes.flight3d.hud.shield: The label over the ship's shield (its health) bar. Keep it short.
notes.flight3d.hud.flagship: The label over the boss's strength bar.
notes.flight3d.complete: The flagship is destroyed: the stage is won. Shown large on screen and as the end screen's title.
notes.flight3d.over.score: The end screen: enemies destroyed and the score, with three spaces between.
notes.flight3d.over.won: The end screen after the win: the flagship is destroyed.
notes.flight3d.over.lost: The end screen after the player's ship is destroyed.
notes.action.roll: A control's name on the controls screen, and in capitals on its touch button: a barrel roll.
notes.action.boost: A control's name: a burst of speed.

brief: The 3D flight slice: a rail shooter like Star Fox 64: the player flies a fighter out over the sea, through waves of enemy fighters and rings, over the enemy's base, into a bay where their flagship waits, then flies free round it. The player's wingman KESTREL calls out on the radio in short, urgent, friendly lines (KESTREL's gender is never given, and the player's neither); the HUD and end screen are short and in capitals.
